sections.name: LazyMount
sections.title: The lazy wrapper
sections.what: Creates a box that fills its parent. It renders its children only while the watcher says the box is near view, using the margin given.
sections.why: Likely reason: each live 3D image holds a graphics context, and browsers can only keep a limited number of them.
sections.watch_out: Children are removed when they leave the margin, so they start again from scratch when they come back.

summary: A wrapper that builds its contents only while they are near the visible part of the screen.
purpose: Limits how many heavy image renderers are active on a page at the same time.
why: The file comment says it keeps the number of live WebGL contexts low on pages with many pixel images. WebGL contexts are a limited browser resource.
how: Watches its own position with a browser observer. When it comes within the margin of the screen it renders its children, and when it moves out of that margin it removes them.
inputs: The children to show, a class name, and a margin (60 percent by default).
outputs: A box sized to its parent that contains the children only while they are near view.
risks: Children are removed when they are far away, so any state or loaded data inside them resets when scrolled back into view. Repeated mounting can cost time.
debug: If images look blank when scrolling, check the margin and whether the children restart. If too many images stay active, check that heavy images sit inside a LazyMount.
